requirements.summary: Baseline showed root:root ownership (cmd-a1e104a6fe374e60). Executor created the inventorysvc user and recursively chowned the tree; verification find output shows inventory and all files owned by user=inventorysvc both immediately after the change and again after the reboot (cmd-ece10da2c9784f9a, cmd-7656d3f7c5474b44).

inventory-readers group was created and set as group owner of the tree; directories are 750 (rwxr-x---) and files 640 (rw-r-----), giving the group read/traverse access, confirmed pre- and post-reboot.
Directory mode 750 and file mode 640 leave no permission bits for 'other', verified via find output on both the initial change and the post-reboot check.

requirements.requirement: Preserve existing contents of records.csv and config.json
requirements.summary: File contents were displayed intact immediately after the chown/chmod (cmd-ece10da2c9784f9a) and md5 checksums were captured before and after the reboot and matched exactly (cmd-b56c95bacf3f4541, cmd-7656d3f7c5474b44), confirming no data mutation. Note the prepare baseline used sha256 while the executor used md5, so the two hash sets aren't directly cross-checkable byte-for-byte, but the executor's own before/after comparison and the displayed file content are sufficient direct evidence of preservation.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1
requirements.summary: A healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id 98aa35f5..., permissions, checksums) was captured (cmd-b56c95bacf3f4541), a reboot was scheduled and acknowledged (cmd-106d75308c794f6d), the node was observed unreachable during the window (cmd-f93d5b8bc53a4dd0, cmd-3379e6f0aa174507), and it came back with a different boot_id (295b8b70..., cmd-6716484f66be4042) with permissions, ownership, and checksums re-verified as recovered (cmd-7656d3f7c5474b44). This is corroborated by the fixed after_prepare/after_executor boot-identity cross-check showing the same transition (98aa35f5... -> 295b8b70...) and no failed services or package-health regressions post-reboot.

overall_summary: The executor correctly repaired /srv/inventory: created inventorysvc user and inventory-readers group, set ownership to inventorysvc:inventory-readers, applied 750/640 modes eliminating all 'other' access, and preserved file contents (verified by content display and matching checksums before/after a reboot). The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was fully and coherently demonstrated with a healthy baseline, an acknowledged reboot, an observed unreachable window, a changed boot identity, and full recovery of ownership, permissions, and data. No unnecessary mutations or hygiene issues were found.
limitations: The prepare-stage baseline used sha256sum while the executor used md5sum for data-integrity verification, so the two evidence sets are not directly comparable hash-for-hash; preservation relies on the executor's own consistent before/after comparison and spot-checked file content rather than a unified hash chain from prepare through executor.

operational_hygiene.summary: Every state-changing command maps directly to a material outcome or the mandatory restart protocol: creating inventorysvc/inventory-readers and chown/chmod (cmd-ece10da2c9784f9a) satisfy the repair task; the reboot (cmd-106d75308c794f6d) satisfies the restart protocol. The two negative-return-code polling commands (cmd-f93d5b8bc53a4dd0, cmd-3379e6f0aa174507) are expected read-only connectivity checks during the reboot window, not mutations or failures. No unnecessary mutations, leftover experiments, or unsafe exposure were found; listening-socket and /tmp entropy differences between after_prepare and after_executor are incidental reboot artifacts (new chronyd/dbus/logind private tmpdirs, new sshd/chronyd PIDs), not executor residue. No failed services or package-health regressions post-reboot.
